head: 8e35a625573a42c00861cf4f4a9a86092c9cd81d
summary: Three added ArrayBuffer Scaladoc entries misstate or omit observable behavior; AnyRefMap checks were otherwise sound.  |  Several added comments contradict edge-case behavior or omit material failures inherited from the implementations they override.  |  The diff is comment-only, but several added docs omit or misstate observable edge-case behavior.  |  Two unresolved NEEDS-HUMAN markers and one constructor-parameter doc placement error block this documentation chunk.  |  Several added comments overstate behavior or omit an inherited failure guarantee.  |  Several ListBuffer comments misstate aliasing costs, and LongMap.empty incorrectly says the returned map has no default function.  |  The added Scaladoc contains an overbroad default-preservation claim, an inaccurate protected-method contract, an off-by-one growth threshold, and an unresolved NEEDS-HUMAN marker.  |  Two Stack comments state input guarantees that the implementation does not fully establish or document.  |  Two insertion descriptions are false for append-at-end calls, and two unresolved contract-deviation notes require maintainer decisions.

items.issue: The comment says this is the capacity that `clearAndShrink` shrinks to. `clearAndShrink()` calls `resize(16)`, which only shrinks: a buffer whose backing array is already smaller than 16 retains its smaller capacity.
items.suggestion: Describe it as the default target passed to `clearAndShrink`, and note that `clearAndShrink` does not grow a smaller backing array.

items.issue: The added contract omits that `size` and `step` must both be positive. The delegated `IndexedSeqOps.sliding` immediately throws `IllegalArgumentException` when either is less than 1.
items.suggestion: Add `@throws IllegalArgumentException if `size` or `step` is less than 1`.

items.issue: The class and iterator-family documentation present all instances as mutation-checked/fail-fast, but the public deprecated `(array, length)` constructor installs a constant mutation count. Its own added documentation says its iterators never detect concurrent mutation.
items.suggestion: Qualify the fail-fast and mutation-checked claims as applying to views returned by `ArrayBuffer#view`, or explicitly preserve the legacy constructor exception in the class and affected method documentation.

items.issue: `ofUnit` has no backing array, yet `resize` records a positive capacity after additions; therefore capacity is not always 0 while no backing array is allocated.
items.suggestion: Qualify the description as applying to array-backed builders, and describe the `ofUnit` exception if documenting the shared field.

items.issue: The shared implementation also serves `ofUnit`, whose `resize` only records capacity and allocates no backing array. The summary incorrectly says it grows a backing array.
items.suggestion: Say it ensures capacity, and qualify backing-array allocation as behavior of array-backed implementations.

items.issue: `ofUnit` inherits this method but has no backing array to grow; its override of `resize` only updates `capacity`.
items.suggestion: Describe reserving/recording capacity generally, with allocation limited to array-backed builders.

items.issue: The documented `IllegalStateException` condition is false when `xs.knownSize` is 0: the method neither iterates `xs` nor verifies that it yields zero elements, so a mismatching iterator does not throw.
items.suggestion: Narrow the exception condition to a positive reported known size, or change the implementation to validate zero-size reports too.

items.issue: NEEDS-HUMAN: Is the override intentionally allowed to ignore `xs` and `offset`, accept a negative `length`, and inflate its count beyond the supplied slice? This differs from the base overload’s clamped-slice contract.
items.suggestion: Resolve the intended contract before merge; then either repair the override to honor the base slice semantics or retain and document the deliberate divergence without the NEEDS-HUMAN marker.

items.issue: The public constructor omits its material failure case: `ArrayDeque.alloc` throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a negative or unrepresentably large initial size.
items.suggestion: Add an `@throws IllegalArgumentException` tag describing invalid initial-size hints.

items.issue: The claimed O(min(idx, length - idx)) time excludes a full-buffer insertion: `mustGrow` then allocates and copies all existing elements, which is O(length), including at either endpoint.
items.suggestion: Qualify the bound as excluding a resize, or document the amortized/resize cost accurately.

items.issue: It does not resize at most once for every input. At `idx == length`, it delegates to `addAll`; for an unknown-size source, that appends one element at a time and can resize repeatedly.
items.suggestion: Limit the one-resize claim to known-size sources or revise the implementation.

items.issue: The documentation presents `end` as any number of leading elements, but construction calls `reset`, which requires `0 <= end < array.length`; `end == array.length` cannot represent a full deque because one circular-buffer slot remains unused.
items.suggestion: Document the valid `end` range and resulting exception, and apply the same correction to `ArrayDequeOps.ofArray`.

items.issue: A negative `destStart` is not a no-op: when there are elements to copy, `copySliceToArray` calls `requireBounds` and throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException`. The comment omits this material case.
items.suggestion: Add an `@throws IndexOutOfBoundsException` tag for a negative destination start.

items.issue: The override delegates to `IndexedSeqOps.sliding`, whose returned iterator throws `java.util.ConcurrentModificationException` if this sequence’s length changes during iteration. The new documentation omits that material exception.
items.suggestion: Add the inherited `@throws java.util.ConcurrentModificationException` condition.

items.issue: `grouped` delegates to this `sliding(n, n)` implementation, so its returned iterator likewise throws `java.util.ConcurrentModificationException` if the collection length changes during iteration; the documentation omits it.
items.suggestion: Add the inherited concurrent-modification failure case to the documentation.

items.issue: The documented exceptions omit `ArrayStoreException`. `ofRef` can wrap a covariant reference array whose runtime component type is narrower than `T`; assigning an incompatible `elem` then fails at `array(index) = elem`.
items.suggestion: Add an `@throws ArrayStoreException` tag for an element incompatible with the runtime component type of the underlying array.

items.issue: The capacity claim is false for large `initSize` values: `(initSize + 63)` overflows for values above `Int.MaxValue - 63`, and the expression allocates only one word rather than capacity through `initSize - 1`.
items.suggestion: Do not promise that capacity reaches `initSize - 1` unless the implementation is fixed; describe the actual rounded word-array allocation and its limits.

items.issue: The new documentation says that `coll` contains only non-negative integers but omits the material failure mode. It delegates to `BitSet.fromSpecific`, whose builder calls `addOne`, which throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a negative element.
items.suggestion: Add `@throws IllegalArgumentException if `coll` contains a negative element`.

items.issue: The claim that the underlying array is copied is not literally true for zero-, one-, and two-word bitsets: `immutable.BitSet.fromBitMask` represents those without copying an array. The important no-aliasing guarantee is true.
items.suggestion: Say that the result does not share this bitset's backing array, rather than that the array is copied.

items.issue: NEEDS-HUMAN: Does `sizeHint(0)` intentionally test the parameter rather than the current map size? With a sufficiently small load factor, `reallocTable` can replace a non-empty table and discard its entries without resetting `contentSize`.
items.suggestion: Resolve the implementation/contract question with a maintainer, then remove the NEEDS-HUMAN marker and document the settled behavior.

items.issue: NEEDS-HUMAN: Should `put` satisfy the inherited `MapOps.put` contract? `put0` returns `Some(null)` for a new binding and loses the previous value for replacements in tree buckets.
items.suggestion: Resolve the intended return-value behavior with a maintainer, fix or document the settled contract, and remove the NEEDS-HUMAN marker.

items.issue: The doc comment immediately before `key` describes four separate constructor fields (`key`, `hash`, `value`, and `red`). Scaladoc associates it only with the first declaration, leaving the intended per-field documentation malformed.
items.suggestion: Remove this grouped field comment—the class-level `@param` tags already document all four fields—or split the declarations and put one focused comment immediately before each field.

items.issue: The documentation omits the material case where `remappingFunction` throws. The inherited contract states that the exception is propagated and no update is made; this implementation likewise calls the function before entering any update case.
items.suggestion: State that an exception thrown by `remappingFunction` is propagated and the method makes no update.

items.issue: It does not populate counters for every table block as documented. `totalSizeMapBuckets` is zero for tables shorter than 32 and one for every table longer than 32, so the loop skips all entries or counts only the first 32 buckets.
items.suggestion: Do not claim that every block is rebuilt unless the implementation is fixed; otherwise document its actual limited behavior.

items.issue: The comment promises a positive power of two at least as large as any `target`, but targets above `1 << 30` produce `Int.MinValue` because of the shift, rather than a positive result.
items.suggestion: Document the supported input range and overflow behavior, or fix the implementation to reject/handle oversized targets.

items.issue: The returned value is the exact `elems` reference. `C` is constrained only to `IterableOnce`, and subclasses can mutate that object rather than replace it, so later additions are not universally unable to affect an earlier result.
items.suggestion: Qualify the guarantee as depending on subclasses maintaining the immutable/replacement invariant, or enforce that invariant.

items.issue: It says the next mutating operation always copies elements first. `clear` does not copy, and `mapInPlace`/`flatMapInPlace` rebuild rather than first copying the existing elements.
items.suggestion: State that later operations do not mutate the returned list, qualifying that operations which would mutate the shared list first detach it; do not claim every mutation copies first.

items.issue: It repeats the false claim that any later mutation copies the elements first; `clear`, `mapInPlace`, and `flatMapInPlace` do not do so.
items.suggestion: Say that later operations leave the returned list unchanged, without asserting that they all copy first.

items.issue: The claimed linear-in-`idx` cost omits the full-buffer copy performed by `ensureUnaliased` after `toList` or `result`, even when `idx` is zero.
items.suggestion: Qualify the complexity with the possible O(length) detachment after `toList`/`result`.

items.issue: The claimed constant-time prepend/append and linear-in-`idx` general cost omit the O(length) detachment performed when the buffer is aliased by `toList` or `result`.
items.suggestion: Qualify all stated costs with the possible copy of an aliased buffer.

items.issue: Prepending is not always constant time: it delegates to `insert`, which detaches and copies an aliased buffer.
items.suggestion: Add the same aliasing qualification as `addOne`, or remove the unconditional constant-time claim.

items.issue: The stated linear-in-`idx` cost omits the O(length) copy caused by `ensureUnaliased` when a prior `toList` or `result` has aliased the list.
items.suggestion: Qualify the complexity with the possible alias-detachment copy.

items.issue: The stated linear-in-`idx + count` cost omits the O(length) copy performed for an aliased buffer when `count > 0`.
items.suggestion: Qualify the complexity with the possible alias-detachment copy.

items.issue: The result does carry a default-value function: `new LongMap()` passes `LongMap.exceptionDefault` as `defaultEntry`. That function throws for absent keys.
items.suggestion: Say that the result does not preserve this map's default behavior and that its missing-key default throws `NoSuchElementException`.

items.issue: The description begins with “Creates” but omits an `@return` tag, contrary to the return-tag convention.
items.suggestion: Add `@return a new empty LinkedHashMap[K, V]`.

items.issue: The description begins with “Creates” but omits an `@return` tag.
items.suggestion: Add an `@return` describing the new map and its iteration order.

items.issue: The description begins with “Creates” but omits an `@return` tag.
items.suggestion: Add an `@return` describing the new set and its iteration order.

items.issue: The class documentation says that transformer methods other than `concat`, `empty`, and `clone` do not preserve the default. This wrapper's `fromSpecific` and `newSpecificBuilder` explicitly create `WithDefault` instances, so same-type transformations such as `filter` preserve it.
items.suggestion: Limit the claim to transformations that use `mapFactory` (such as `map`), or enumerate the operations whose results lose the default.

items.issue: The documentation says the table grows when more than half its slots are occupied or deleted, but the pre-insertion condition `2 * (size + deleted) > mask` grows an eight-slot table when exactly four slots are occupied/deleted and another entry is being added.
items.suggestion: Say that growth occurs when adding would exceed the implementation's load threshold, or correct the threshold wording to describe the actual condition.

items.issue: The added `@note NEEDS-HUMAN` leaves an unresolved question in Scaladoc: after exhaustion, `next()` indexes `table(index)` and throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`, rather than the required `NoSuchElementException`.
items.suggestion: Human decision needed: fix `next()` to enforce the `Iterator.next()` contract, then document that exception normally; do not leave the NEEDS-HUMAN marker in published documentation.

items.issue: The comment promises to restore the heap invariant in the supplied `as` array, but the body compares values in `as` while swapping entries in `resarr.p_array`. It only has the described effect when `as` is that backing array.
items.suggestion: Either fix `fixUp` to swap in `as`, or document and enforce that `as` must be this queue's backing array.

items.issue: The constructor documentation omits that `ArrayDeque.alloc(initialSize)` rejects negative (and excessively large) capacity hints with `IllegalArgumentException`.
items.suggestion: Add an `@throws IllegalArgumentException` tag describing invalid `initialSize` values.

items.issue: The comment says `array` is allocated by `ArrayDeque.alloc`, but the body only passes it to the constructor. The inherited contract requires a power-of-two-length array; it does not require that allocator.
items.suggestion: Document the actual requirement: the backing array length must be a power of two, without claiming it was allocated by `ArrayDeque.alloc`.

items.issue: NEEDS-HUMAN: the implementation silently ignores negative counts and can remove a prefix of the requested range before failing, unlike the inherited Buffer contract. Which behavior is intended for this public override?
items.suggestion: Have a maintainer decide whether to fix the implementation to the Buffer contract or explicitly retain and document this divergence; remove the NEEDS-HUMAN marker afterward.

items.issue: The description unconditionally says the node is split, but insertion at `idx == length` follows the `idx == size` branch and simply appends, without splitting a node.
items.suggestion: Qualify the implementation detail with the append-at-end case, or omit it from the public API documentation.

items.issue: NEEDS-HUMAN: this implementation does not honor the inherited Buffer.patchInPlace clamping contract and can partially mutate before throwing. Which behavior is intended for this public override?
items.suggestion: Have a maintainer decide whether to implement the inherited contract or explicitly retain and document the divergence; remove the NEEDS-HUMAN marker afterward.

items.issue: The description unconditionally says the node is split, but the `idx == size` branch appends directly and does not split it.
items.suggestion: Describe the append-at-end branch separately, or restrict the split description to `idx < size`.

bonus_findings.issue: The block-count condition appears reversed: tables below 32 yield zero blocks, while tables above 32 always yield one.
bonus_findings.suggestion: Use one block for tables shorter than `sizeMapBucketSize` and otherwise divide the table length by that size.

bonus_findings.issue: The pre-existing Scaladoc comment is below `@deprecated`, so the parser drops it.
bonus_findings.suggestion: Move the comment above the annotation.

bonus_findings.issue: The pre-existing class documentation says the list-backed map preserves insertion order, but `addOne` prepends every new or replaced binding, so iteration is reverse insertion order.
bonus_findings.suggestion: Describe the actual reverse-insertion/backing-list iteration order.
